g.text: Decision D2 · Is Attempt its own aggregate or an entity inside Task?
decision-code-D2 · generated from code.json · confidence medium

svg.text: Rationale: 04 S7 is a preservation row: the reap ends the attempt and requeues the task in 1 transaction before any signal. With 1 aggregate per transaction, the attempt must be inside Task. Verification stays apart so the verifier is the only module that can produce a VerifiedVerdict (define N1).
Would flip if: The ledger allows a multi-aggregate transaction as an explicit exception for the reap
Would flip if: Attempts must carry large state such as transcripts

g.text: 3 aggregates as discover proposes: Task, Attempt, Verification.
+ Attempt rows of sub-orchestrators fit without a task
− 04 S7 needs the attempt end and the task requeue in 1 transaction, which crosses 2 aggregates
! A crash between the 2 writes loses the requeue (the #216 bug)
Task holds its Attempts and the Lease; Verification stays its own aggregate.
+ A task has at most max_attempts attempts, so the aggregate stays small
+ Verification runs long checks outside the task transaction
− Sub-orchestrator attempts (task_id null) are not part of this aggregate and are written by ideas
! Task grows if attempts keep transcripts; they must keep only ids and outcomes
aggregate: Attempt entity, Lease valueaggregate: Attempt entity, Lease value
1 Task aggregate that also holds the verification state.
− A 20 min check holds the task aggregate
− The only-the-verifier-sets-done rule has no module seam
! define N1 is harder to prove
20 min, outside tx20 min, outside tx
aggregate: attempts, lease, checks, judge findingsaggregate: attempts, lease, checks, judge findings
